why: Confidence is not ignoring symptoms. A useful self-management plan helps you decide when to continue, when to modify, and when to seek support.

slides.title: Continue
slides.content: A familiar, expected response that settles as planned may be compatible with continuing the activity or recovery plan while monitoring the pattern.

slides.title: Modify
slides.content: Adjust range, load, speed, duration, position, rest, or task strategy when the current dose repeatedly interferes with function or recovery.

slides.title: Seek Support
slides.content: Seek appropriate assessment for new, severe, progressive, unusual, or concerning symptoms—or when the plan is not helping you move forward.

slides.title: Use Context
slides.content: One sensation rarely provides the whole answer. Consider what changed, what the task required, how you responded, and whether the pattern is familiar.

slides.title: Try This Today
slides.content: Choose one current activity and write what would tell you to continue, modify, or contact your practitioner. If you are unsure about concerning symptoms, seek appropriate advice.
